data.description:
## Summary

Every `aws_ssm_parameter` managed by `infra/terraform` stores its parameter value in CLEARTEXT in
the remote terraform state, including 20+ `SecureString` secrets. `terraform state pull` renders
them all in plain text to anyone who can read the state backend, which defeats the SecureString/KMS
boundary those parameters were chosen for.

## Evidence (read-only, no value displayed)

Discovered while verifying `colourless-hasteless-lamb`. `terraform state pull` from
`infra/terraform` (S3 backend `rebar-tfstate-896586841071`, key `rebar/prod/terraform.tfstate`,
us-east-1) and digesting each `aws_ssm_parameter` instance's `attributes.value` against the digest
of the literal `CHANGEME` placeholder shows every one holds a REAL value, not the placeholder:

    /rebar/prod/anthropic-api-key             SecureString  REAL(len=108)
    /rebar/prod/ci-gerrit-ssh-key             SecureString  REAL(len=399)
    /rebar/prod/gerrit-admin-password         SecureString  REAL(len=32)
    /rebar/prod/gerrit-ssh-host-ed25519-key   SecureString  REAL(len=398)
    /rebar/prod/github-oauth-client-secret    SecureString  REAL(len=40)
    /rebar/prod/github-replication-deploy-key SecureString  REAL(len=418)
    /rebar/prod/opcert-ed25519-key            SecureString  REAL(len=410)
    /rebar/prod/rebar-bot-signing-key         SecureString  REAL(len=432)
    /rebar/prod/jira-api-token                SecureString  REAL(len=192)
    ... 23 aws_ssm_parameter instances in total, all REAL

Only digests and lengths were computed; no value was printed, logged, or written anywhere.

## Why the existing mitigation does not cover this

The repo's precedent for operator-seeded secrets is `value = "CHANGEME"` +
`lifecycle { ignore_changes = [value] }`. That correctly stops terraform WRITING a real value from
the repo — no credential is in git, which is the property it was designed for. It does NOT stop
terraform READING the live value into state: on refresh (and on `import` adoption) the provider
populates `attributes.value` from AWS. So the placeholder in the `.tf` is not a placeholder in the
state, and the two are routinely confused.

This is PRE-EXISTING and project-wide, NOT introduced by the Jira wiring — `jira-api-token` is one
of many in the same posture, and secrets created by terraform with `CHANGEME` show real values too
because refresh overwrote them. Filed separately so the Jira ticket is not scope-crept.

## Partial existing controls, worth crediting

- The S3 backend sets `encrypt = true`, so the state is encrypted AT REST.
- The blast radius is therefore "anyone with read access to the state bucket / the terraform role",
  not "anyone on the internet".

The gap is that this collapses the secret tier down to the state-bucket ACL: a principal who can
run `terraform plan` can read the Gerrit admin password, the opcert Ed25519 signing key and the
rebar-bot signing key in cleartext, none of which they need.

## Suggested directions (to be evaluated, not pre-decided)

1. `ephemeral`/write-only arguments — the AWS provider's `value_wo` + `value_wo_version` on
    `aws_ssm_parameter` (provider >= 5.79, terraform >= 1.11) keeps the value out of state entirely.
    Current pins are terraform 1.15.8 and aws 5.100.0, so both floors are already met.
2. Stop managing seeded secret VALUES in terraform at all — declare only existence/type via a
    `data` source or drop the `value` argument where the provider permits it.
3. If neither is viable, tighten and document the state-bucket ACL as an explicit secret-tier
    boundary, with a KMS CMK and an access policy, so the exposure is a recorded decision rather
    than an accident.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The mechanism by which real values enter state is documented, with a cited reproduction.
- [ ] A decision is recorded on which of the directions above is taken, including "accept, with a
      tightened and documented state-bucket boundary".
- [ ] If a code direction is chosen: no `SecureString` parameter's real value appears in
      `terraform state pull` output, asserted by a test or a documented operator check that
      compares digests rather than printing values.
- [ ] No credential value is printed, logged, or committed by the fix or by its verification.
data.title: Terraform state stores every SSM SecureString value in cleartext, collapsing the secret tier to the state-bucket ACL
